column1: vincent-luis-kona-heat-preparation,"How did Vincent Luis prepare for the heat at Kona?","¿Cómo se preparó Vincent Luis para el calor de Kona?","Vincent Luis won the 2026 IRONMAN World Championship in Kona in 7:47:27, on a day that reached 88°F at the airport. By his own account, he started heat work with hot baths and sauna in January and February, added easy rides and runs in the heat before IRONMAN Texas in April, and 3 weeks out was doing IRONMAN-pace sessions in a heat chamber at 32°C and 80% humidity. On race day he said he took about 145 g of carbs an hour on the bike and about 100 g an hour on the run.","Vincent Luis ganó el Campeonato Mundial IRONMAN 2026 en Kona en 7:47:27, en un día que llegó a 88°F en el aeropuerto. Según contó él mismo, empezó a trabajar el calor con baños calientes y sauna en enero y febrero, sumó rodadas y trotes suaves con calor antes del IRONMAN Texas de abril, y 3 semanas antes hacía sesiones a ritmo IRONMAN en una cámara de calor a 32°C y 80% de humedad. El día de la carrera dijo que tomó unos 145 g de carbohidratos por hora en la bici y unos 100 g por hora corriendo.","One elite athlete (n = 1). His prep numbers are self-reported, from interviews after the race. He has no connection to Raceproof.
## What did Kona ask of him?

Official IRONMAN results: 1st in 7:47:27, with a 48:31 swim, a 4:15:42 bike and a 2:38:36 run. Gustav Iden was 2nd in 7:49:02, 1:35 back. Luis came off the bike sixth, 6:04 behind Magnus Ditlev (Tri247), and took the lead at the mile 21 aid station (Slowtwitch race report).

The heat and humidity were the main demand. At Kona International Airport (PHKO) the high was 88°F. At 6:53 am it was already 79°F with 88% humidity, and from 6 am to 5 pm humidity ran from 61% to 88%. The airport isn't on the course. IRONMAN's course page lists a 2026 high of 88°F (31°C) and average water of 79°F (26°C).

column1: ## How did he train for the heat?
- **Passive heat first.** ""Since January February I really started with passive [heat], so hot bath, sauna and everything"" ([All-In Triathlon](https://youtu.be/TXpXTfYTn28), uploaded Oct 12, 2026
column2: the episode is sponsored by Precision Fuel & Hydration).

column1: - **Active heat before Texas.** Before IRONMAN Texas in April, he added ""easy rides, easy runs"" in the heat (same interview). He said he raced Texas ""for obvious reasons with early qualifying, racing a bit in the heat and humidity"" ([ProTriNews](https://youtu.be/6Mpl1odkY5g), recorded Oct 11, 2026).

- **Race pace in the heat chamber.** ""3 weeks out of Kona I could do Iron Man pace sessions in the heat chamber at 32 degrees and 80% humidity,"" running efforts of about 8 minutes at 3:30 per km at a heart rate of 150, while also at altitude (All-In Triathlon).

- **Heat and altitude together.** He arrived in Font-Romeu ""maybe 10 to 12 weeks before the race"" and did ""altitude training and heat training... both in the heat chamber at altitude"" ([The Triathlon Hour](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uY61pcBHsyQ), Oct 18, 2026).
- **Timing.** He skipped the race in Nice because ""four weeks out of the race... is the exact moment you want to clock big weeks and you want to do the heat prep"" (The Triathlon Hour).

He also checked his core temperature. On a day of almost 40°C, his core temperature rose to about 39.5°C during 5 x 5 minutes at threshold, by his own estimate, and came back down to 39°C at IRONMAN pace. He read that as a sign he ""was ready for the heat"" (The Triathlon Hour).

column1: ## What does the research say about his heat prep?

**Hot baths and sauna.** In a controlled trial, 6 days of 40-minute hot baths after runs improved a 5 km test in 33°C by 4.9%, with no change at 18°C ([Zurawlew et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1111/sms.12638)), a small study of 17 men. If you have a heart condition, high or low blood pressure, take blood pressure medication, are pregnant, or have had heat illness, talk to your doctor before trying hot baths or sauna.

**Training in the heat.** An expert consensus recommends repeated exercise in the heat over 1 to 2 weeks, and using cooling during the event ([Racinais et al. 2015](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2015-094915)). A meta-analysis of 96 articles found the biggest adaptations after more than 14 days ([Tyler et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-016-0538-5)).

**Keeping it to race day.** About 2.5% of heat adaptations are lost for every day without heat ([Daanen et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-017-0808-x)). His heat chamber work 3 weeks out kept heat going close to the race. More in our article on [how long heat acclimation takes](https://raceproof.ai/blog/heat-acclimation-how-long).

**Weighing in.** He weighed himself ""before and after every big sessions"" to track fluid loss (The Triathlon Hour). After 8 days of heat training, sweat rate rose 0.23 to 0.42 L an hour in 22 trained men ([McDonald et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1249/MSS.0000000000004190)).
## How did he fuel and pace in the heat?

He said he took 40 g of carbs right before the bike, ""around 145"" g an hour on the bike and ""around 100 grams an hour"" on the run, ""which is what we practiced in training"". He planned 1.4 to 1.5 L of fluid an hour on the bike and took ""1.6 or 1.7"" (All-In Triathlon). He used IRONMAN Frankfurt and Boise to keep ""practicing nutrition"" (ProTriNews). His nutrition partner is 6d Sports Nutrition.

At the aid stations, IRONMAN's own race video shows him drinking one cup of water, pouring a second inside his suit and putting ice in his cap. ""I was taking everything I could,"" he said (The Triathlon Hour).

His pacing plan was patience: ""I really wanted to have two matches left for the run"" (ProTriNews). In a review of 70.3 studies, conservative bike pacing that spares glycogen was linked to a better final run ([von Känel-Cordoba et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0352506)), an observed link, not proof.

**What carries over.** The order and timing. Heat has its own window: build it 6 to 2 weeks out, then keep some heat to race day. Gut training starts about 12 weeks out, with race-level carbs by 4 to 6 weeks out.

**What doesn't.** A heat chamber near home, altitude camps and elite physiology. His 145 g/h is not a target. Guidelines set up to 90 g/h for efforts over 2.5 to 3 hours ([2016 position statement](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26917108/)). A 2026 review says the ceiling could rise to 120 g/h for trained athletes and that higher is unproven ([Morton et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tjnut.2026.101442)

- **Ritmo de carrera en la cámara de calor.** ""3 semanas antes de Kona podía hacer sesiones a ritmo IRONMAN en la cámara de calor a 32 grados y 80% de humedad"", con tramos de unos 8 minutos corriendo a 3:30 por km con una frecuencia cardíaca de 150, mientras además estaba en altura (All-In Triathlon).

- **El momento.** No corrió en Niza porque ""cuatro semanas antes de la carrera... es el momento exacto en que quieres hacer semanas grandes y quieres hacer la preparación para el calor"" (The Triathlon Hour).

También revisó su temperatura corporal. En un día de casi 40°C, su temperatura interna subió a unos 39.5°C durante 5 x 5 minutos a umbral, según su propia estimación, y bajó a 39°C a ritmo IRONMAN. Lo tomó como señal de que ""estaba listo para el calor"" (The Triathlon Hour).

column1: ## ¿Qué dice la ciencia sobre su preparación para el calor?

**Baños calientes y sauna.** En un ensayo controlado, 6 días de baños calientes de 40 minutos después de correr mejoraron una prueba de 5 km a 33°C en 4.9%, sin cambios a 18°C ([Zurawlew et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1111/sms.12638)), un estudio chico de 17 hombres. Si tienes una condición cardíaca, presión alta o baja, tomas medicamentos para la presión, estás embarazada o tuviste un golpe de calor, habla con tu médico antes de probar baños calientes o sauna.

**Entrenar con calor.** Un consenso de expertos recomienda ejercicio repetido con calor durante 1 a 2 semanas, y enfriarse durante la competencia ([Racinais et al. 2015](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2015-094915)). Un metaanálisis de 96 artículos encontró las mayores adaptaciones después de más de 14 días ([Tyler et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-016-0538-5)).

**Mantenerlo hasta la carrera.** Cerca del 2.5% de las adaptaciones al calor se pierde por cada día sin calor ([Daanen et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-017-0808-x)). Su trabajo en la cámara 3 semanas antes mantuvo el calor cerca de la carrera. Más en nuestro artículo sobre [cuánto tarda la aclimatación al calor](https://raceproof.ai/blog/heat-acclimation-how-long).

**Pesarse.** Se pesaba ""antes y después de cada sesión grande"" para seguir la pérdida de líquido (The Triathlon Hour). Tras 8 días de entrenamiento con calor, la tasa de sudoración subió de 0.23 a 0.42 L por hora en 22 hombres entrenados ([McDonald et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1249/MSS.0000000000004190)).

Dijo que tomó 40 g de carbohidratos justo antes de la bici, ""unos 145"" g por hora en la bici y ""unos 100 gramos por hora"" corriendo, ""que es lo que practicamos en el entrenamiento"". Planeó 1.4 a 1.5 L de líquido por hora en la bici y tomó ""1.6 o 1.7"" (All-In Triathlon). Usó el IRONMAN de Frankfurt y el de Boise para seguir ""practicando la nutrición"" (ProTriNews). Su marca de nutrición es 6d Sports Nutrition.

En los abastecimientos, el video de carrera del propio IRONMAN lo muestra tomando un vaso de agua, echándose otro dentro del traje y poniendo hielo en su gorra. ""Tomaba todo lo que podía"", dijo (The Triathlon Hour).

Su plan de ritmo fue la paciencia: ""quería guardar dos fósforos para la carrera a pie"" (ProTriNews). En una revisión de estudios de 70.3, un ritmo conservador en la bici, que ahorra glucógeno, se relacionó con una mejor carrera a pie ([von Känel-Cordoba et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0352506)): una relación observada, no una prueba.

**Lo que sirve.** El orden y el momento. El calor tiene su propia ventana: constrúyelo entre 6 y 2 semanas antes y mantén algo de calor hasta el día de la carrera. El entrenamiento del estómago empieza unas 12 semanas antes, con los carbohidratos de carrera entre 4 y 6 semanas antes.

**Lo que no.** Una cámara de calor cerca de casa, campamentos en altura y una fisiología de élite. Sus 145 g/h no son una meta. Las guías fijan hasta 90 g/h para esfuerzos de más de 2.5 a 3 horas ([postura conjunta de 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26917108/)). Una revisión de 2026 dice que el techo podría subir a 120 g/h en atletas entrenados y que más arriba no está probado ([Morton et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tjnut.2026.101442)
column2: varios autores tienen vínculos con Science in Sport). En 8 maratonistas de élite que tomaron 120 g/h, las molestias digestivas fueron máximas ([Ravikanti et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1152/japplphysiol.00665.2025), financiado por Science in Sport).
